title: Frame rain and cicada pulse as equal living forces
objective: Keep the brief's listener question audible in form, lyrics, melody, delivery, and arrangement.
decision: Treat rain as an irregular continuous/tailing field and cicadas as a dry cyclic repeated-note resistance; move from rain-dominant perception to coexistence without victory.
rationale: The two different behaviors can remain identifiable across the song and directly answer whether they share one night rather than decorate a generic rock track.

alternatives.reason: It would name the scene without making the two forces interact.
It would erase the hot, immediate, resistant pulse required by the brief.

expected_audible_effect: The listener should track rain and cicadas as different rhythmic envelopes that become simultaneously necessary.
next_step: Verify the choice in the next materialization or audition stage.

constraints: Intent brief is sole creative authority
No corpus or reference melody access

title: Use a 48-bar arc with one 20-bar chorus anchor
objective: Fit the 50–70 second target while giving the two-force interaction enough time to become audible.
decision: Use 4-bar intro, 8-bar verse, 8-bar pulse discovery, 20-bar coexistence chorus, and 8-bar shared-night outro.
rationale: At 190 BPM the 48 bars last about 60.63 seconds, and the 20-bar chorus is about 25.26 seconds for the required anchor ladder.

alternatives.reason: At 190 BPM it is too short for a 20–30 second creative closure.
The brief asks for high-BPM identity; density and half-time perception can provide contrast instead.

expected_audible_effect: Rain is established before IA enters; the cicada pulse earns foreground status; the long anchor can drive and then clear without leaving the section.
next_step: Verify the choice in the next materialization or audition stage.

observations: 48 bars at 190 BPM calculate to 60.632 seconds before renderer tail handling.

title: Hold 190 BPM while alternating driving and half-time perception
objective: Create physical rock momentum without turning every layer or lyric into continuous fast subdivisions.
decision: Use constant 190 BPM in 4/4; intro/verse and the internal chorus clearing imply half-time, while discovery and primary chorus use a driving backbeat.
rationale: The preferred BPM is honored exactly; perceived-speed contrast comes from snare placement, note density, and phrase space.

alternatives.reason: It weakens the brief's preferred urgent pulse without solving arrangement density.
It would crowd consonants and flatten the specified dynamic contrast.

expected_audible_effect: The track should feel hot and immediate, with sections that breathe at the same tempo rather than sounding mechanically relentless.
next_step: Verify the choice in the next materialization or audition stage.

observations: Canonical tempo is 190 BPM at measure 0 with no tempo drift.

title: Use D-Dorian color with functional dominant handoffs
objective: Keep the night restless and wet without collapsing into pure melancholy or generic major-key summer cheer.
decision: Center D minor/D Dorian, foreground G major as a flash of humid clarity, use Bb/C lateral motion, and reserve A/Asus4 for transitions and formal handoffs.
rationale: The raised sixth color gives heat and openness while the D-minor center retains immediacy; one chord per bar keeps harmonic function legible at 190 BPM.

alternatives.reason: It risks a uniform melancholy the brief explicitly avoids.
It would push the scene toward generic cheerful summer pop.

expected_audible_effect: G-major bars should flash through the wet D-minor field; A-function bars should energize handoffs without dominating every cadence.
next_step: Verify the choice in the next materialization or audition stage.

constraints: Hot, wet, restless, flashes of clarity

title: Compose distinct phrase roles around one transformed two-force identity
objective: Make adjacent entries, contours, peaks, motion, and cadences serve discovery, confrontation, clearing, and coexistence.
decision: Verse phrases use delayed plateaus/valleys; pulse discovery uses terraces and a bounded fourth; the chorus rain call descends from a downbeat while the cicada answer repeats higher and enters as an answer; later returns preserve repeated-note/duration identity while changing peak placement, range, and cadence.
rationale: The identity survives as rhythm and named-call balance rather than as repeated identical rise/fall arches.

alternatives.option: Every line rises to a late peak then falls
alternatives.reason: It would flatten phrase roles and violate the brief's anti-template boundary.
It would make the high BPM itself the only source of intensity.

expected_audible_effect: Rain and cicada clauses should be recognizable by different entry/contour behaviors, while the outro call is heard as related but changed.

title: Use explicit Japanese readings, measured rests, and semantic duration
objective: Keep the original Japanese surface intelligible at 190 BPM while making prosody part of the musical argument.
decision: Allocate every non-sokuon mora explicitly, keep leading/tail rests as cells, connect most internal gates, lengthen named forces and releases, and attach the small っ in 重なって to the following /t/ within its note.
rationale: The plan puts consonants ahead of selected strong beats, gives vowels the beat, and avoids uniform micro-gaps or invented small-っ phonemes.

alternatives.reason: It would hide semantic duration and melisma/rest decisions.
The V3 Japanese chart provides no such token; attach-next is declared and must be auditioned.

expected_audible_effect: Named forces and final clauses should remain intelligible and weighted even when the band drives.

title: Shape IA_ROCKS with selective forward articulation and a receding timbre arc
objective: Make intensity arise from delivery changes rather than constant brightness or mastering level.
decision: Use lower verse opening/BRI, rising pre-chorus consonant energy, a chorus DYN/opening/BRI/CLE arch, an internal clearing reduction, one bounded chorus scoop, and vibrato only on three earned sustained notes including the final line.
rationale: Distinct parameter arcs trace the dramatic motion and preserve Japanese consonants while keeping the ending present rather than defeated.

alternatives.reason: It would erase contrast and violate the brief's must-avoid list.
It would turn emphasis into a default style rather than earned semantic delivery.

expected_audible_effect: The lead should move from close/wet to forward/resistant, then ease while retaining articulation; only selected targets should scoop or bloom.

title: Separate rain continuity from cicada cyclic resistance
objective: Make the two scene forces audible through orchestration while retaining physical rock momentum and Japanese consonant space.
decision: Use five functional band tracks: mixed-feel drums, root/fifth bass with Dorian lower-neighbor approaches, sparse power-chord rhythm guitar, left irregular descending/tailing clean-guitar rain, and right dry repeated-note cicada attacks grouped 3+3+2. Thin drums and both signatures without removing them in the internal clearing.

alternatives.reason: Literal effects would bypass the requested translation into rhythm, register, articulation, and orchestration.
It would mask consonants and flatten mixed-feel contrast.
It adds no necessary function beyond the existing harmonic/rain roles.

rationale: The preflight located eight unsingable mora durations, five consonant risks, and two short vibratos. Timing redistribution fixes performance risk without changing surface text, reading, phrase start, or form.

rationale: Track-level gain, high-pass/notch choices, side placement, and section dynamics perform the balance work before loudness normalization. The master needs only 1.3 dB peak reshaping and no LRA change, so the final lift does not replace the composition's dynamics.
